objectives.description: Comprehension: reading and understanding two short passages in Efik.
Composition/letter writing: essay types including narrative, descriptive, argumentative, expository, dialogue, debate, letter writing (approximately 300 words).

Sound system: vowels and consonants — production in terms of place and manner of articulation, basic phonetic and phonemic classifications; syllable structure — the way consonants and vowels combine in words; sound processes e.g. vowel harmony, assimilation, elision, deletion, etc.; distribution of sounds; adaptation of loanwords; tone and intonation — high tone, low tone, falling tone, rising tone.

Grammar: word structure and word formation — root, affixes (prefix, suffix), compounding, borrowing, reduplication, etc.; word classes — noun, verbs, adverbs, pronouns, adjectives, etc.; grammatical categories — number, person, tense, negation, etc.; phrases and clauses — types and functions; the structure and types of sentences.
Translation: translation exercises between Efik and English.
Oral literature: prose (folktales, legends, proverbs, riddles, etc.), poetry (songs, ballads), drama (traditional drama) — set books covering different genres.
Written literature — prose, poetry, drama: set books covering different genres.
Customs (Edu Uwem): occupational activities (fishing, weaving, market); good upbringing and its benefits; food preparation and serving etiquette; libation (uduọk mmịn).

Institutions (Nsionsio nka): family (ubon/ekpuk) — family kinship systems; worship (edu ukpono/se ekponode) — Abasi, Ndem, Ibọk, Mbukpo; proverbs (mme nke); secret society (Ubọñ/mme ndedịbe nka ke Efik).
